drhp.business: Lagnam Spintex Limited manufactures cotton yarn from cotton at a single integrated spinning facility at A 51-53, RIICO Growth Centre, Hamirgarh, Bhilwara District, Rajasthan. The Company states it manufactures only one product, cotton yarn, and that segment/product-wise details are therefore not applicable. Yarn counts range from Ne 4 to Ne 40 and are sold to apparel and garment manufacturers, denim, terry-towel, home-textile and industrial-fabric users in India and in export markets.

risks.note: Cotton is the primary raw material for yarn and is an agricultural produce whose supply and quality are subject to forces of nature i.e. monsoon. The Company states any increase in raw cotton prices makes things difficult for the industry, resulting in weak demand and thin margins, and that availability of raw cotton at reasonable prices is crucial for the spinning industry. Compounding this, untimely rainfall in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana has damaged crops and farmers are shifting to more profitable crops, reducing cultivated area.
risks.risk: Raw cotton price and availability - single agricultural input, monsoon-dependent

risks.note: 'High Import Dependency: Due to low local output, reliance on imported cotton is rising (up 85% YoY in 5M FY2026), increasing costs for manufacturers.' The mitigation cited - a temporary exemption on cotton import duties - was valid only until December 2025, so the cost cushion is stated as expiring.

The US imposed a 50% effective tariff on Indian apparel exports in August 2025, trickling down to demand for Indian cotton yarn, with Indian exporters discounting to hold market share and narrowing spinner margins. Separately, RoDTEP export rebates were cut from 3.4% to 1.7% of FOB value, directly impacting export profitability. Lagnam's own export revenue fell ~7.5% in FY2025-26 and export volumes fell to 9,868 MT from 10,335 MT, with margin pressure in H1 attributed to subdued demand in key European markets impacted by US tariff developments.
risks.risk: US tariff shock and reduced export incentives compressing export profitability

risks.note: Spinners' margins are expected to contract by 50-100 basis points in FY2026, particularly in the second half. Average cotton yarn contributions dropped from Rs. 103/kg in H1 FY2026 to Rs. 96/kg in November 2025.
risks.risk: Industry margin contraction and falling yarn contribution

risks.note: The Company states the high rate of interest is affecting the financial performance of the textile industry, and that spinning, being more capital intensive, requires huge long-term and short-term working-capital funds; it calls on Government to provide cheap finance so the industry remains financially viable. Structurally relevant to Lagnam, whose borrowings are backed by personal guarantees of the director and a corporate guarantee of a related company.
risks.risk: Capital intensity plus high interest rates

risks.note: Structural concentration disclosed indirectly rather than labelled as a risk: 'As the Company is manufacturing only the one product i.e. Cotton Yarn, Therefore, segment/product-wise details are not applicable', and the whole manufacturing base is one facility at Hamirgarh, Bhilwara, Rajasthan. There is no product, process or geographic diversification to absorb a cotton-cycle or site-level shock.

Indian textiles face stiff competition from Bangladesh, Taiwan and other emerging economies and from countries with lower tariff rates; the MD&A also concedes India's runner-up position faces 'stiff chances of being taken away by smaller countries like Vietnam and Bangladesh'. Separately, increasing availability of cheaper synthetic alternatives (polyester/nylon) continues to threaten demand for cotton-based products, and one stated Indian demand driver is an explicit 'shift from cotton to man-made fiber'.
risks.risk: Competitive displacement by lower-cost countries and by synthetic fibre

risks.note: Geopolitical instability in neighbouring markets like Bangladesh has disrupted trade, challenging growth in export volumes; and although a recovery in exports to China is expected early in the year, fluctuations in Chinese demand remain a constant risk factor. Currency movement is separately flagged - exchange rate fluctuations affect export pricing and profitability for Indian yarn exporters.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption in export corridors and Chinese demand volatility
